reason: Prior measurements show the three-buffer Strassen wrapper lost all ten paired runs, so its variants rank low; they retain its seven products and FP32 rounding risks. The 32-row classical panel is a directly testable change to the active path, though its ZA and store changes raise correctness risk. The loop-control rewrite is narrower and lower risk but may not affect a bottleneck. One-allocation and vectorized-packing changes target limited costs with no evidence those costs caused prior regressions. Fused transpose could remove scratch traffic but rereads A 16 times and adds complex register work. Tail splitting targets general sizes, not the fixed n=512 timing.
